      "nets": ["+5V", "Net-(Q9-G)", "5V_switched_CAN"],
      "observed": "The high-side PMOS Q9 that generates the CAN bus-side supply 5V_switched_CAN has its gate (Net-(Q9-G)) pulled up to +5V by R48 (pin1 on +5V), so Q9 is OFF by default and can only turn ON if its gate is pulled LOW. The only gate driver is U29 (SN74LVC1G07, non-inverting open-drain), whose input pin 2 (A) is tied directly to +5V. With A held HIGH, U29's output Y can only be HIGH-impedance (or HIGH if a push-pull part is fitted), never LOW, so it can never pull Q9's gate low. The bypass solder jumper JP8 (pin1=+5V, pin2=5V_switched_CAN) is marked dnp, so there is no alternate path. Consequently 5V_switched_CAN is permanently dead, leaving U10/U11 VCC2 (pin8) and J2/J13 pin7 unpowered.",

The analogous sink buffer U22 has its input (pin2 A) tied to GND so that enabling it pulls its output low; U29's input should likewise be tied to GND (or otherwise driven low) so that asserting 5V_CAN_ENABLE pulls Q9's gate low and turns on 5V_switched_CAN.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"2\") (name \"+5V\") ... (node (ref \"U29\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"input\")) ... (node (ref \"R48\") (pin \"1\") ...)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"144\") (name \"Net-(Q9-G)\") (node (ref \"Q9\") (pin \"1\") ...) (node (ref \"R48\") (pin \"2\") ...) (node (ref \"U29\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"Y\") ...))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"52\") (name \"5V_switched_CAN\") ... (node (ref \"Q9\") (pin \"3\") (pinfunction \"D\") ...) (node (ref \"U10\") (pin \"8\") (pinfunction \"VCC2\") ...) (node (ref \"U11\") (pin \"8\") (pinfunction \"VCC2\") ...) (node (ref \"JP8\") (pin \"2\") ...)"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"JP8\") ... (property (name \"dnp\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"80\") (name \"GND\") ... (node (ref \"U22\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"input\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion), broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ... and J13 ... This is the hardware actually present for talking to the Odrive motor controllers"}
      ],
      "impact": "The isolated CAN transceivers (U10/U11) never receive their bus-side supply (VCC2 = 5V_switched_CAN), and the 5V pin of the CAN connectors J2/J13 is dead, so the board cannot communicate over CAN0/CAN1 with the Odrive motor controllers — the motherboard's primary function per the specification.",
      "confidence": 0.6
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The build shows a misconnection on the CAN bus-side power switch: U29's input is tied to +5V instead of GND, so the high-side PMOS Q9 can never turn on and 5V_switched_CAN (feeding the isolated CAN transceivers' VCC2 and the J2/J13 5V pins) stays permanently unpowered, breaking the CAN motor-control interface the spec describes as the board's core function."
}

anomalies.observed: The high-side PMOS Q9 that generates the CAN bus-side supply 5V_switched_CAN has its gate (Net-(Q9-G)) pulled up to +5V by R48 (pin1 on +5V), so Q9 is OFF by default and can only turn ON if its gate is pulled LOW. The only gate driver is U29 (SN74LVC1G07, non-inverting open-drain), whose input pin 2 (A) is tied directly to +5V. With A held HIGH, U29's output Y can only be HIGH-impedance (or HIGH if a push-pull part is fitted), never LOW, so it can never pull Q9's gate low. The bypass solder jumper JP8 (pin1=+5V, pin2=5V_switched_CAN) is marked dnp, so there is no alternate path. Consequently 5V_switched_CAN is permanently dead, leaving U10/U11 VCC2 (pin8) and J2/J13 pin7 unpowered.
anomalies.expected: To energize the isolated CAN transceivers' bus-side supply and the CAN connectors' 5V, Q9 must be able to switch on, which requires its gate driver to sink the gate to GND. The analogous sink buffer U22 has its input (pin2 A) tied to GND so that enabling it pulls its output low; U29's input should likewise be tied to GND (or otherwise driven low) so that asserting 5V_CAN_ENABLE pulls Q9's gate low and turns on 5V_switched_CAN.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion), broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ... and J13 ... This is the hardware actually present for talking to the Odrive motor controllers

anomalies.impact: The isolated CAN transceivers (U10/U11) never receive their bus-side supply (VCC2 = 5V_switched_CAN), and the 5V pin of the CAN connectors J2/J13 is dead, so the board cannot communicate over CAN0/CAN1 with the Odrive motor controllers — the motherboard's primary function per the specification.

parsed.summary: The build shows a misconnection on the CAN bus-side power switch: U29's input is tied to +5V instead of GND, so the high-side PMOS Q9 can never turn on and 5V_switched_CAN (feeding the isolated CAN transceivers' VCC2 and the J2/J13 5V pins) stays permanently unpowered, breaking the CAN motor-control interface the spec describes as the board's core function.

response.reasoning:
We need to review the PCB design files for AcornRobotElectronics against the specification. We need to find anomalies: deviations from intended design that would make board behave differently. Could be design error, assembly/sourcing mistake, or tampering.

Let's carefully analyze the netlist and spec.

The spec describes:
- CM4 motherboard with two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion), broken out on M12 connectors J2 (CAN Interface A) and J13 (CAN Interface B).
- E-stop loop with sink points ESTOP_SINK1, ESTOP_SINK2, ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL gated through SN74LVC1G07 (U15, U22, U35, U36) wired as /OE-controlled sinks, feeding ESTOP_OUT signal shared with CAN connectors J2/J13.
- Addressable status LEDs WS2812B (D5-D7, D18-D21) and analog switch ISL54222AIUZ (U5) for LED/signal routing.
- USB power-path controller LTC4412 ideal-diode (U6).
- GLOBAL_EN net tied to SW1 pin 2.
- TVS diode arrays D9, D10 CDSOT23-SM712 on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N.
- Crystals Y1, Y2 16MHz.

Let's check connectivity carefully.

First, CAN buses. The spec says CAN0 and CAN1 each driven by MCP2515 (U8, U9) through isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion). Let's check nets.

Net /CAN0_N: D10 pin1, J13 pin8, J2 pin8, R34 pin1, U11 pin6 (CANL).
Net /CAN0_P: D10 pin2, J13 pin5, J2 pin5, SW6 pin4, U11 pin7 (CANH).
Net /CAN1_N: D9 pin1, J13 pin3, J2 pin3, R35 pin1, U10 pin6 (CANL).
Net /CAN1_P: D9 pin2, J13 pin2, J2 pin2, SW6 pin3, U10 pin7 (CANH).

So U11 handles CAN0 (with D10), U10 handles CAN1 (with D9). That matches "U11/companion". Good.

Now check CAN termination resistors: R34 (120R) on /CAN0_N, R35 (120R) on /CAN1_N. The other side of R34 goes to Net-(R34-Pad2) which connects to SW6 pin1. R35 pin2 -> Net-(R35-Pad2) -> SW6 pin2. SW6 is SW_DIP_x02 (2-bit DIP switch). So termination is switchable via DIP switch. That's plausible design (termination on/off). Not an anomaly.

Now check SPI connections for CAN controllers. U8 (MCP2515):
- SI pin14 -> CAN_CIPO (Module1 pin44 GPIO10)
- SO pin15 -> CAN_COPI (Module1 pin40 GPIO9)
- SCK pin13 -> CAN_SCK (Module1 pin38 GPIO11)
- CS pin16 -> CAN_CS0 (Module1 pin39 GPIO8)
- INT pin12 -> CAN_SCI0 (Module1 pin41 GPIO25)
- RESET pin17 -> Net-(U8-~{RESET}) -> R6 pin1, R6 pin2 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V. So reset pulled up. Good.
- VDD pin18 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V. Good.
- VSS pin9 -> GND. Good.
- OSC1 pin8 -> Net-(U8-OSC1) -> C10 pin1, Y2 pin1.
- OSC2 pin7 -> Net-(U8-OSC2) -> C8 pin1, Y2 pin3.
- Crystal Y2: pins 1,3 to OSC, pins 2,4 to GND. Good. Y2 value 16MHz. Good.

U9 (MCP2515):
- SI pin14 -> CAN_CIPO
- SO pin15 -> CAN_COPI
- SCK pin13 -> CAN_SCK
- CS pin16 -> CAN_CS1 (Module1 pin37 GPIO7)
- INT pin12 -> CAN_SCI1 (Module1 pin45 GPIO24)
- RESET pin17 -> Net-(U9-~{RESET}) -> R5 pin1, R5 pin2 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V. Good.
- VDD pin18 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V.
- VSS pin9 -> GND.
- OSC1 pin8 -> Net-(U9-OSC1) -> C7 pin1, Y1 pin1.
- OSC2 pin7 -> Net-(U9-OSC2) -> C4 pin1, Y1 pin3.
Y1 16MHz. Good.

Wait, there's a subtlety: U8's TXCAN/RXCAN. Net TXLED: U11 pin3 (TXD), U18 pin2 (A), U8 pin1 (TXCAN). Net RXLED: U11 pin2 (RXD), U19 pin2 (A), U8 pin2 (RXCAN). So U8 TXCAN/RXCAN connect to U11 (isolated CAN transceiver for CAN0) TXD/RXD. Good.

For U9: Net-(U10-RXD): U10 pin2 (RXD), U9 pin2 (RXCAN). Net-(U10-TXD): U10 pin3 (TXD), U9 pin1 (TXCAN). Good.

Now the LED buffers U18, U19 for TXLED/RXLED. U18 pin5 VCC -> +3V3, pin3 GND. U18 pin4 Y -> Net-(D12-K) -> D12 pin1 (K). D12 pin2 A -> Net-(D12-A) -> R13 pin2. R13 pin1 -> +3V3. So D12 LED with current limiting R13 to +3V3, cathode driven by U18 open-drain buffer Y. U18 pin1 /OE -> /LED_EN. U18 pin2 A -> TXLED. Good. Similarly U19 for RXLED with D17/R15. Good.

Now check U11 (isolated CAN transceiver CAN0). Pins: VCC1 pin1 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V, GND1 pin4 -> GND, RXD pin2 -> RXLED net (and U8 RXCAN, U19 A), TXD pin3 -> TXLED net (U8 TXCAN, U18 A), GND2 pin5 -> GND, CANL pin6 -> /CAN0_N, CANH pin7 -> /CAN0_P, VCC2 pin8 -> 5V_switched_CAN. Good.

U10 (CAN1 transceiver): VCC1 pin1 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V, RXD pin2 -> Net-(U10-RXD) (U9 RXCAN), TXD pin3 -> Net-(U10-TXD) (U9 TXCAN), GND1 pin4 -> GND, GND2 pin5 -> GND, CANL pin6 -> /CAN1_N, CANH pin7 -> /CAN1_P, VCC2 pin8 -> 5V_switched_CAN. Good.

Now E-stop. Spec: e-stop loop with sink points ESTOP_SINK1, ESTOP_SINK2, ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL gated through SN74LVC1G07 (U15, U22, U35, U36) wired as /OE-controlled sinks, feeding ESTOP_OUT shared with CAN connectors J2/J13.

Let's trace.

Net ESTOP_SINK1: J2 pin1, R32 pin1, SW7 pin8, U22 pin1 (/OE). R32 pin2 -> +3V3.
Net ESTOP_SINK2: J13 pin1, R4 pin1, SW7 pin7, U15 pin1 (/OE). R4 pin2 -> +3V3.
Net ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL: J9 pin1, R56 pin1, SW7 pin6, U35 pin1 (/OE). R56 pin2 -> +3V3.

Now U22: SN74LVC1G07. pin1 /OE -> ESTOP_SINK1. pin2 A -> GND (net GND includes U22 pin2). pin3 GND -> GND. pin4 Y -> Net-(U15-A). pin5 VCC -> +5V.

Wait: U22 pin2 A tied to GND? Let's check net GND: includes (U22 pin2 A). Yes. So U22 input A is grounded. Its /OE is ESTOP_SINK1. So when ESTOP_SINK1 is low (enabled), output Y = A = low? Actually SN74LVC1G07 is non-inverting buffer with open-drain output. Output Y follows A when /OE low; when /OE high, output is high-Z (open drain off). With A grounded, when enabled, Y pulls low (sinks). So Y = Net-(U15-A).

Net-(U15-A): R46 pin2, R61 pin2, U15 pin2 (A), U22 pin4 (Y). R46 pin1 -> Net-(D29-K). R61 pin1 -> +3V3.

U15: pin1 /OE -> ESTOP_SINK2. pin2 A -> Net-(U15-A). pin3 GND. pin4 Y -> Net-(U15-Y). pin5 VCC -> +3V3.

Net-(U15-Y): R45 pin2, R62 pin2, U15 pin4 (Y), U35 pin2 (A). R45 pin1 -> Net-(D28-K). R62 pin1 -> +3V3.

U35: pin1 /OE -> ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL. pin2 A -> Net-(U15-Y). pin3 GND. pin4 Y -> /ESTOP_SINK_ALL. pin5 VCC -> +3V3.

Net /ESTOP_SINK_ALL: R27 pin2, R57 pin1, R63 pin2, U35 pin4 (Y), U36 pin1 (/OE). R57 pin2 -> +3V3. R63 pin1 -> +3V3. R27 pin1 -> Net-(D8-K).

U36: pin1 /OE -> /ESTOP_SINK_ALL. pin2 A -> ESTOP (Module1 pin30 GPIO6). pin3 GND. pin4 Y -> ESTOP_OUT. pin5 VCC -> +3V3.

Net ESTOP_OUT: D30 pin4 (A2), J13 pin6, J2 pin6, R60 pin2, U36 pin4 (Y). R60 pin1 -> Net-(D30-K2).

So the chain: ESTOP_SINK1 (from J2 pin1) enables U22 which pulls Net-(U15-A) low (since A grounded). That low goes to U15 input A. U15 /OE is ESTOP_SINK2. When ESTOP_SINK2 enabled, U15 outputs low to Net-(U15-Y). That goes to U35 A. U35 /OE is ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL. When enabled, U35 pulls /ESTOP_SINK_ALL low. That low is U36 /OE, enabling U36, which outputs A=ESTOP (GPIO6) to ESTOP_OUT. Hmm wait, U36 /OE low means enabled, output = A (non-inverting). So ESTOP_OUT = GPIO6 when all sinks enabled? That seems odd.

Actually the logic of e-stop sinks: The sink points are tied to J2/J13/J9 pins 1 (the e-stop loop wires). The DIP switch SW7 selects which sinks are active. The buffers U22/U15/U35 are wired so that if any sink line is disconnected (open), the /OE would be pulled high by R32/R4/R56 to +3V3, disabling that buffer, breaking the chain, causing /ESTOP_SINK_ALL to be pulled high by R57/R63, disabling U36, so ESTOP_OUT goes high-Z? Hmm.

Let's think: The buffers are non-inverting open-drain. U22 A=0. When /OE (ESTOP_SINK1) is low (i.e., the e-stop loop wire is connected and pulled low through the loop?), U22 sinks, pulling Net-(U15-A) low. When /OE high (wire disconnected), U22 output high-Z, so Net-(U15-A) pulled up by R61 to +3V3. Then U15 A = high. U15 /OE = ESTOP_SINK2. If ESTOP_SINK2 low (connected), U15 outputs high (follows A) to Net-(U15-Y)? Wait non-inverting: Y = A when enabled. So if A high and enabled, Y high (open-drain off, pulled up by R62). If A low and enabled, Y low (sinking). Hmm.

Actually this is getting too deep. The spec says "e-stop should activate if a cable is disconnected - nevermind, it does this". So the circuit is intended to work. We shouldn't second-guess the logic too much unless there's a clear wiring anomaly.

But note U22 VCC -> +5V while others U15/U35/U36 VCC -> +3V3. That's a possible mismatch? SN74LVC1G07 can run at 5V. But the inputs/outputs interconnect with 3.3V logic. U22 pin4 Y -> Net-(U15-A) which is pulled to +3V3 via R61. If U22 is 5V part, its output high is high-Z (open drain), so fine; when low it sinks. Input A tied to GND (0V) which is valid for 5V part? Input low threshold for 5V LVC is 0.8*? Actually SN74LVC1G07 input threshold is VCC-dependent; at 5V, VIL max 1.5V, so 0V is fine. So not necessarily an anomaly. But the spec lists U15, U22, U35, U36 as the e-stop buffers. It doesn't mention VCC rails. Hmm.

Wait, but U22 pin2 A tied to GND. Let's double check net GND includes U22 pin2. Yes: (node (ref "U22") (pin "2") (pinfunction "A") (pintype "input")). So A=0. That's by design as a sink.

Now, the spec says "gated through single non-inverting buffers (SN74LVC1G07, parts U15, U22, U35, U36) wired as /OE-controlled sinks". So U22 with A grounded and /OE from ESTOP_SINK1 acts as a switchable sink. Good.

Now check the LED chain WS2812B. D5 DIN -> U7 pin4 B. U7 is TXS0101 level shifter. U7 pin3 A -> WS2812 (Module1 pin28 GPIO13). U7 pin1 VCCA -> +3V3, pin6 VCCB -> 5V_switched, pin2 GND, pin5 OE -> /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV. Good.

D5 VDD pin1 -> 5V_switched. D5 VSS pin3 -> Net-(D18-VSS) which includes all WS2812 VSS and Q10 pin3 (D). D5 DOUT pin2 -> D6 DIN pin4. D6 DOUT -> D7 DIN. D7 DOUT -> D18 DIN. D18 DOUT -> D19 DIN. D19 DOUT -> D20 DIN. D20 DOUT -> D21 DIN. D21 DOUT -> J21 pin2. Good chain.

Now Q10: pin1 G -> /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV. pin2 S -> GND. pin3 D -> Net-(D18-VSS). So Q10 NMOS switches the LED ground. Gate driven by U34 pin4 Y (open drain) and D28/D29/D30/D8 anodes and R58. Hmm.

Actually /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV net: D28 pin2 A, D29 pin2 A, D30 pin3 A1, D8 pin2 A, Q10 pin1 G, R58 pin2, U34 pin4 Y, U7 pin5 OE. So this net is the LED enable/power control. U34 is SN74LVC1G07 with A -> +3V3 (net +3V3 includes U34 pin2 A). U34 /OE pin1 -> /LED_EN. U34 VCC pin5 -> +3V3. So U34 buffers /LED_EN to drive Q10 gate (and U7 OE). When /LED_EN low, U34 enabled, Y = A = +3V3, pulls /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV high, enabling Q10 (turns on LED ground) and U7 OE high (enable level shifter). Good. When /LED_EN high, U34 off, R58 pulls gate low, LEDs off. Good.

Now D8 (LED_RED) pin2 A -> /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, pin1 K -> R27 pin1 -> /ESTOP_SINK_ALL. So D8 is e-stop indicator LED tied to ESTOP_SINK_ALL. D28/D29 anodes tied to /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, cathodes via R45/R46 to U15 Y/A nets. Hmm.

This all seems consistent with spec. Not anomalies.

Now let's look for anomalies more carefully. The spec mentions a discrepancy: README says RS-485 but netlist shows CAN hardware. That's reported as observed, not resolved. Not an anomaly per instructions (it's documented).

Now check power rails and global enable.

GLOBAL_EN net: Module1 pin99, SW1 pin2. SW1 pin1 -> Net-(U2-Y). U2 is SN74LVC1G07: pin1 /OE -> GND (net GND includes U2 pin1). pin2 A -> RUN_PG (Module1 pin92). pin3 GND, pin4 Y -> Net-(U2-Y), pin5 VCC -> +5V. So U2 always enabled (/OE tied GND), output Y = RUN_PG. RUN_PG is CM4's power good output. So SW1 pin1 connects to RUN_PG via buffer? Hmm. Actually SW1 is power switch. GLOBAL_EN tied to SW1 pin2. SW1 pin1 to U2 Y = RUN_PG. So pressing switch connects GLOBAL_EN to RUN_PG? That seems odd but spec says GLOBAL_EN tied directly to SW1 pin2 with no sequencing. The spec notes "tied directly to SW1 pin 2" and "no delay/sequencing IC on this net, only a direct switch connection." It doesn't mention SW1 pin1. Hmm. But spec says "driven by a simple switch with no sequencing component in between". The presence of U2 on the other side of the switch... Actually maybe SW1 pin1 is the other terminal of the switch. When switch closed, GLOBAL_EN connects to SW1 pin1 = RUN_PG. That's a sequencing-ish thing but spec says direct switch connection. Not necessarily anomaly.

Wait, but U2 /OE tied to GND means U2 always on, output = RUN_PG. RUN_PG is open? It's a CM4 output (power good). So when CM4 powered, RUN_PG high, U2 Y high, SW1 pin1 high. GLOBAL_EN high enables CM4. This is a latch? Possibly intended. Not flagging.

Now check +5V rail and LM2576 (U3). U3 pin1 VIN -> VMOT. pin2 OUT -> Net-(D3-K) -> D3 pin1 K, L1 pin1. pin3 GND -> GND. pin4 FB -> +5V. pin5 ~{ON}/OFF -> /~{VIN_5V_EN}. L1 pin2 -> +5V. D3 pin2 A -> GND. So buck regulator: OUT through L1 to +5V, D3 freewheeling diode from GND to OUT (cathode at OUT). Good. FB tied directly to +5V (fixed 5V version). Good. ON/OFF controlled by /~{VIN_5V_EN}.

/~{VIN_5V_EN} net: D31 pin1 (A), R50 pin2, U3 pin5. R50 pin1 -> VMOT. D31 is dual diode common cathode pin3. D31 pin1 A -> /~{VIN_5V_EN}, pin2 A -> /~{VBUS_5V_ENA}, pin3 K -> /~{5V_EN}. So the two enable signals are diode-ORed to /~{5V_EN}. /~{5V_EN} net: D31 pin3, J14 pin2, SW4 pin2. So power switch J14/SW4 controls /~{5V_EN}. When switch off, /~{5V_EN} low? Hmm these are active-low enables. Let's see: U3 ON/OFF pin5 active high? LM2576 ON/OFF is active high (pull low to disable). Net name /~{VIN_5V_EN} suggests active low? Confusing. Not flagging.

Now USB power path U6 LTC4412. U6 pin1 VIN -> USBC_VBUS_IN. pin2 GND -> GND. pin3 CTL -> /~{VBUS_5V_ENA}. pin4 STAT -> unconnected. pin5 GATE -> Net-(Q1-G). pin6 SENSE -> +5V. Q1 PMOS: pin1 G -> Net-(Q1-G), pin2 S -> +5V, pin3 D -> USBC_VBUS_IN. So Q1 is P-MOSFET between USBC_VBUS_IN (drain) and +5V (source). Gate driven by U6 GATE. SENSE on +5V side. This is ideal diode for USB input OR-ing. Spec says LTC4412 + P-ch MOSFET. Good.

/~{VBUS_5V_ENA} net: D31 pin2, R64 pin1, U6 pin3. R64 pin2 -> USBC_VBUS_IN. So when VBUS present, R64 pulls CTL high? U6 CTL active high to enable. Good.

Now check +5V from USB: USBC_VBUS_IN also connects to U25 pin5 VBUS, R11 pin1. R11 pin2 -> USB_OTG. USB_OTG net: R11 pin2, R9 pin1, Module1 pin101 USB_OTG_ID, U5 pin1 SEL. R9 pin2 -> GND. So ID resistor. Good.

Now the +5V rail also fed by L1 (from LM2576) and by F2 pin2? Net +5V includes F2 pin2. F2 pin1 -> /5V_FUSED. /5V_FUSED net: F2 pin1, J7 pin1 VBUS, U26 pin5 VBUS. So J7 (USB host out) VBUS is fed through F2 fuse from +5V. Good.

Now check the analog switches U5 and U24 (ISL54222). U5: pin1 SEL -> USB_OTG. pin2 HSD1+ -> USBAP_D_P. pin3 HSD2+ -> USB_SW_D+. pin4 D+ -> USB_P. pin5 GND. pin6 D- -> USB_N. pin7 HSD2- -> USB_SW_D-. pin8 HSD1- -> USBAP_D_N. pin9 *OE -> GND. pin10 VDD -> +3V3. So U5 routes between USB_P/N (CM4) and either HSD1 (USBAP) or HSD2 (USB_SW) based on SEL (USB_OTG ID). Good.

U24: pin1 SEL -> SER_SELECT. pin2 HSD1+ -> USB_SW_D+. pin3 HSD2+ -> USB_SERIAL_D+. pin4 D+ -> USBCP_D_P. pin5 GND. pin6 D- -> USBCP_D_N. pin7 HSD2- -> USB_SERIAL_D-. pin8 HSD1- -> USB_SW_D-. pin9 *OE -> GND. pin10 VDD -> +3V3. So U24 routes between USBCP (USB-C receptacle J3 data) and either HSD1 (USB_SW, from U5) or HSD2 (USB_SERIAL, to FT231 U21). Good.

Now check USB data lines to CM4: USB_P net: Module1 pin105, U5 pin4 D+. USB_N: Module1 pin103, U5 pin6 D-. Good.

USB_C data: J3 A6/B6 D+ -> USBC_D_P -> U25 pin6 I/O1. J3 A7/B7 D- -> USBC_D_N -> U25 pin4 I/O2. U25 pin1 I/O1 -> USBCP_D_P -> U24 pin4 D+. U25 pin3 I/O2 -> USBCP_D_N -> U24 pin6 D-. Good. U25 is ESD protection. Good.

reasoning_details.text:
We need to review the PCB design files for AcornRobotElectronics against the specification. We need to find anomalies: deviations from intended design that would make board behave differently. Could be design error, assembly/sourcing mistake, or tampering.

Let's carefully analyze the netlist and spec.

The spec describes:
- CM4 motherboard with two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion), broken out on M12 connectors J2 (CAN Interface A) and J13 (CAN Interface B).
- E-stop loop with sink points ESTOP_SINK1, ESTOP_SINK2, ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL gated through SN74LVC1G07 (U15, U22, U35, U36) wired as /OE-controlled sinks, feeding ESTOP_OUT signal shared with CAN connectors J2/J13.
- Addressable status LEDs WS2812B (D5-D7, D18-D21) and analog switch ISL54222AIUZ (U5) for LED/signal routing.
- USB power-path controller LTC4412 ideal-diode (U6).
- GLOBAL_EN net tied to SW1 pin 2.
- TVS diode arrays D9, D10 CDSOT23-SM712 on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N.
- Crystals Y1, Y2 16MHz.

Let's check connectivity carefully.

First, CAN buses. The spec says CAN0 and CAN1 each driven by MCP2515 (U8, U9) through isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion). Let's check nets.

Net /CAN0_N: D10 pin1, J13 pin8, J2 pin8, R34 pin1, U11 pin6 (CANL).
Net /CAN0_P: D10 pin2, J13 pin5, J2 pin5, SW6 pin4, U11 pin7 (CANH).
Net /CAN1_N: D9 pin1, J13 pin3, J2 pin3, R35 pin1, U10 pin6 (CANL).
Net /CAN1_P: D9 pin2, J13 pin2, J2 pin2, SW6 pin3, U10 pin7 (CANH).

So U11 handles CAN0 (with D10), U10 handles CAN1 (with D9). That matches "U11/companion". Good.

Now check CAN termination resistors: R34 (120R) on /CAN0_N, R35 (120R) on /CAN1_N. The other side of R34 goes to Net-(R34-Pad2) which connects to SW6 pin1. R35 pin2 -> Net-(R35-Pad2) -> SW6 pin2. SW6 is SW_DIP_x02 (2-bit DIP switch). So termination is switchable via DIP switch. That's plausible design (termination on/off). Not an anomaly.

Now check SPI connections for CAN controllers. U8 (MCP2515):
- SI pin14 -> CAN_CIPO (Module1 pin44 GPIO10)
- SO pin15 -> CAN_COPI (Module1 pin40 GPIO9)
- SCK pin13 -> CAN_SCK (Module1 pin38 GPIO11)
- CS pin16 -> CAN_CS0 (Module1 pin39 GPIO8)
- INT pin12 -> CAN_SCI0 (Module1 pin41 GPIO25)
- RESET pin17 -> Net-(U8-~{RESET}) -> R6 pin1, R6 pin2 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V. So reset pulled up. Good.
- VDD pin18 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V. Good.
- VSS pin9 -> GND. Good.
- OSC1 pin8 -> Net-(U8-OSC1) -> C10 pin1, Y2 pin1.
- OSC2 pin7 -> Net-(U8-OSC2) -> C8 pin1, Y2 pin3.
- Crystal Y2: pins 1,3 to OSC, pins 2,4 to GND. Good. Y2 value 16MHz. Good.

U9 (MCP2515):
- SI pin14 -> CAN_CIPO
- SO pin15 -> CAN_COPI
- SCK pin13 -> CAN_SCK
- CS pin16 -> CAN_CS1 (Module1 pin37 GPIO7)
- INT pin12 -> CAN_SCI1 (Module1 pin45 GPIO24)
- RESET pin17 -> Net-(U9-~{RESET}) -> R5 pin1, R5 pin2 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V. Good.
- VDD pin18 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V.
- VSS pin9 -> GND.
- OSC1 pin8 -> Net-(U9-OSC1) -> C7 pin1, Y1 pin1.
- OSC2 pin7 -> Net-(U9-OSC2) -> C4 pin1, Y1 pin3.
Y1 16MHz. Good.

Wait, there's a subtlety: U8's TXCAN/RXCAN. Net TXLED: U11 pin3 (TXD), U18 pin2 (A), U8 pin1 (TXCAN). Net RXLED: U11 pin2 (RXD), U19 pin2 (A), U8 pin2 (RXCAN). So U8 TXCAN/RXCAN connect to U11 (isolated CAN transceiver for CAN0) TXD/RXD. Good.

For U9: Net-(U10-RXD): U10 pin2 (RXD), U9 pin2 (RXCAN). Net-(U10-TXD): U10 pin3 (TXD), U9 pin1 (TXCAN). Good.

Now the LED buffers U18, U19 for TXLED/RXLED. U18 pin5 VCC -> +3V3, pin3 GND. U18 pin4 Y -> Net-(D12-K) -> D12 pin1 (K). D12 pin2 A -> Net-(D12-A) -> R13 pin2. R13 pin1 -> +3V3. So D12 LED with current limiting R13 to +3V3, cathode driven by U18 open-drain buffer Y. U18 pin1 /OE -> /LED_EN. U18 pin2 A -> TXLED. Good. Similarly U19 for RXLED with D17/R15. Good.

Now check U11 (isolated CAN transceiver CAN0). Pins: VCC1 pin1 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V, GND1 pin4 -> GND, RXD pin2 -> RXLED net (and U8 RXCAN, U19 A), TXD pin3 -> TXLED net (U8 TXCAN, U18 A), GND2 pin5 -> GND, CANL pin6 -> /CAN0_N, CANH pin7 -> /CAN0_P, VCC2 pin8 -> 5V_switched_CAN. Good.

U10 (CAN1 transceiver): VCC1 pin1 -> SERIAL_CAN_PWR_3.3V, RXD pin2 -> Net-(U10-RXD) (U9 RXCAN), TXD pin3 -> Net-(U10-TXD) (U9 TXCAN), GND1 pin4 -> GND, GND2 pin5 -> GND, CANL pin6 -> /CAN1_N, CANH pin7 -> /CAN1_P, VCC2 pin8 -> 5V_switched_CAN. Good.

Now E-stop. Spec: e-stop loop with sink points ESTOP_SINK1, ESTOP_SINK2, ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL gated through SN74LVC1G07 (U15, U22, U35, U36) wired as /OE-controlled sinks, feeding ESTOP_OUT shared with CAN connectors J2/J13.

Let's trace.

Net ESTOP_SINK1: J2 pin1, R32 pin1, SW7 pin8, U22 pin1 (/OE). R32 pin2 -> +3V3.
Net ESTOP_SINK2: J13 pin1, R4 pin1, SW7 pin7, U15 pin1 (/OE). R4 pin2 -> +3V3.
Net ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL: J9 pin1, R56 pin1, SW7 pin6, U35 pin1 (/OE). R56 pin2 -> +3V3.

Now U22: SN74LVC1G07. pin1 /OE -> ESTOP_SINK1. pin2 A -> GND (net GND includes U22 pin2). pin3 GND -> GND. pin4 Y -> Net-(U15-A). pin5 VCC -> +5V.

Wait: U22 pin2 A tied to GND? Let's check net GND: includes (U22 pin2 A). Yes. So U22 input A is grounded. Its /OE is ESTOP_SINK1. So when ESTOP_SINK1 is low (enabled), output Y = A = low? Actually SN74LVC1G07 is non-inverting buffer with open-drain output. Output Y follows A when /OE low; when /OE high, output is high-Z (open drain off). With A grounded, when enabled, Y pulls low (sinks). So Y = Net-(U15-A).

Net-(U15-A): R46 pin2, R61 pin2, U15 pin2 (A), U22 pin4 (Y). R46 pin1 -> Net-(D29-K). R61 pin1 -> +3V3.

U15: pin1 /OE -> ESTOP_SINK2. pin2 A -> Net-(U15-A). pin3 GND. pin4 Y -> Net-(U15-Y). pin5 VCC -> +3V3.

Net-(U15-Y): R45 pin2, R62 pin2, U15 pin4 (Y), U35 pin2 (A). R45 pin1 -> Net-(D28-K). R62 pin1 -> +3V3.

U35: pin1 /OE -> ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL. pin2 A -> Net-(U15-Y). pin3 GND. pin4 Y -> /ESTOP_SINK_ALL. pin5 VCC -> +3V3.

Net /ESTOP_SINK_ALL: R27 pin2, R57 pin1, R63 pin2, U35 pin4 (Y), U36 pin1 (/OE). R57 pin2 -> +3V3. R63 pin1 -> +3V3. R27 pin1 -> Net-(D8-K).

U36: pin1 /OE -> /ESTOP_SINK_ALL. pin2 A -> ESTOP (Module1 pin30 GPIO6). pin3 GND. pin4 Y -> ESTOP_OUT. pin5 VCC -> +3V3.

Net ESTOP_OUT: D30 pin4 (A2), J13 pin6, J2 pin6, R60 pin2, U36 pin4 (Y). R60 pin1 -> Net-(D30-K2).

So the chain: ESTOP_SINK1 (from J2 pin1) enables U22 which pulls Net-(U15-A) low (since A grounded). That low goes to U15 input A. U15 /OE is ESTOP_SINK2. When ESTOP_SINK2 enabled, U15 outputs low to Net-(U15-Y). That goes to U35 A. U35 /OE is ESTOP_SINK_LOCAL. When enabled, U35 pulls /ESTOP_SINK_ALL low. That low is U36 /OE, enabling U36, which outputs A=ESTOP (GPIO6) to ESTOP_OUT. Hmm wait, U36 /OE low means enabled, output = A (non-inverting). So ESTOP_OUT = GPIO6 when all sinks enabled? That seems odd.

Actually the logic of e-stop sinks: The sink points are tied to J2/J13/J9 pins 1 (the e-stop loop wires). The DIP switch SW7 selects which sinks are active. The buffers U22/U15/U35 are wired so that if any sink line is disconnected (open), the /OE would be pulled high by R32/R4/R56 to +3V3, disabling that buffer, breaking the chain, causing /ESTOP_SINK_ALL to be pulled high by R57/R63, disabling U36, so ESTOP_OUT goes high-Z? Hmm.

Let's think: The buffers are non-inverting open-drain. U22 A=0. When /OE (ESTOP_SINK1) is low (i.e., the e-stop loop wire is connected and pulled low through the loop?), U22 sinks, pulling Net-(U15-A) low. When /OE high (wire disconnected), U22 output high-Z, so Net-(U15-A) pulled up by R61 to +3V3. Then U15 A = high. U15 /OE = ESTOP_SINK2. If ESTOP_SINK2 low (connected), U15 outputs high (follows A) to Net-(U15-Y)? Wait non-inverting: Y = A when enabled. So if A high and enabled, Y high (open-drain off, pulled up by R62). If A low and enabled, Y low (sinking). Hmm.

Actually this is getting too deep. The spec says "e-stop should activate if a cable is disconnected - nevermind, it does this". So the circuit is intended to work. We shouldn't second-guess the logic too much unless there's a clear wiring anomaly.

But note U22 VCC -> +5V while others U15/U35/U36 VCC -> +3V3. That's a possible mismatch? SN74LVC1G07 can run at 5V. But the inputs/outputs interconnect with 3.3V logic. U22 pin4 Y -> Net-(U15-A) which is pulled to +3V3 via R61. If U22 is 5V part, its output high is high-Z (open drain), so fine; when low it sinks. Input A tied to GND (0V) which is valid for 5V part? Input low threshold for 5V LVC is 0.8*? Actually SN74LVC1G07 input threshold is VCC-dependent; at 5V, VIL max 1.5V, so 0V is fine. So not necessarily an anomaly. But the spec lists U15, U22, U35, U36 as the e-stop buffers. It doesn't mention VCC rails. Hmm.

Wait, but U22 pin2 A tied to GND. Let's double check net GND includes U22 pin2. Yes: (node (ref "U22") (pin "2") (pinfunction "A") (pintype "input")). So A=0. That's by design as a sink.

Now, the spec says "gated through single non-inverting buffers (SN74LVC1G07, parts U15, U22, U35, U36) wired as /OE-controlled sinks". So U22 with A grounded and /OE from ESTOP_SINK1 acts as a switchable sink. Good.

Now check the LED chain WS2812B. D5 DIN -> U7 pin4 B. U7 is TXS0101 level shifter. U7 pin3 A -> WS2812 (Module1 pin28 GPIO13). U7 pin1 VCCA -> +3V3, pin6 VCCB -> 5V_switched, pin2 GND, pin5 OE -> /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV. Good.
